response:
I ran the scan and then opened the three files it points at to confirm the mechanism.

## What's happening

One finding explains the whole report: **`crime_00001` Cross-Language Type Drift** (high, confidence 0.75).

`Plan` is declared as a *closed set* twice, by hand, in two languages:

| | declared tiers |
|---|---|
| `packages/api/billing/plans.py:10` (Python `str, Enum`) | `free`, `pro`, `team`, `scale` |
| `packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10` (TS union) | `free`, `pro`, `enterprise` |

Only `free` and `pro` are shared. The newest tiers — `team` and `scale` — exist **only** on the API side. The API is the canonical list (its own docstring says so: *"The canonical list of tiers lives here. The web client keeps its own copy… and the two have drifted"*).

So the failure is asymmetric, exactly as your users report it:

1. A user is provisioned on `scale`. The API accepts and stores it — `Plan.SCALE` is a legal enum member, `seats_for` maps it to 50, `POST /api/teams/{id}/plan` echoes it back happily.
2. The web app fetches that workspace. `getWorkspace()` returns `Promise<Workspace>`, and `Workspace.plan` is typed `"free" | "pro" | "enterprise"`.
3. Whatever narrows the response to that union — a zod/valibot enum built from the same list, a `switch` with a throwing `default`, a plan→label lookup — has no `scale` case. The user is rejected with a validation error.

The TS union itself is erased at runtime, so the union *line* isn't the thing throwing; it's the source of truth that the web's runtime guard was written from. That's why the error surfaces only in the browser and never in the API's own tests.

The `enterprise` entry is the mirror-image bug waiting to happen: it's TS-only, so if the UI ever sends `enterprise` to `POST /api/teams/{id}/plan`, the Python side takes it as a bare `str`, and `seats_for` silently falls through to `.get(plan, 1)` → **1 seat**, no error. That fails soft, which is worse.

## Why the upgrade path is also broken

Two route-drift findings mean that even after you add `scale` to the web union, changing a plan still won't work:

- **`crime_00003`** — `workspace-client.ts:34` calls `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan`; `routes.py:25` declares that path as `POST`. The path exists, so this is a **405**, not a 404 — very easy to misread as a permissions bug.
- **`crime_00005`** — `workspace-client.ts:23` calls `POST /api/workspaces`, a path no backend route declares (the backend has `POST /api/teams`). That's a **404** that reads like a data problem.

Also note `workspace-client.ts:28` and `:34` fetch the *literal string* `"/api/teams/:id/plan"` — the `:id` is never interpolated. Whatever `id` you pass is discarded.

## Why nobody caught it

**`crime_00004`** Concept Alias Drift is the reason this survived review: the same concept is `team` in Python and `workspace` in TypeScript across all 3 files. Anyone (human or agent) grepping `team` finds only the backend half; grepping `workspace` finds only the frontend half. Neither search shows you that there are two competing definitions of `Plan`. `test_gap` is 1.0 on every finding here — there is no test that crosses the boundary.

## Fix

Immediate, to unblock users:

1. Add `"team" | "scale"` to the TS union and to the web-side runtime validator; decide whether `enterprise` is dead (delete it) or was renamed to `team`/`scale` (map it).
2. Change `changeWorkspacePlan` to `POST`, and interpolate the id: `` fetch(`/api/teams/${id}/plan`, { method: "POST" }) `` — same for `workspaceSeats`.
3. Point `createWorkspace` at `POST /api/teams`.

## What stops it recurring

Patching the union just resets the clock — the same drift reappears at the next tier. The structural fix is to stop hand-maintaining two copies of a closed set:

- **Make the Python enum the single source and generate the TS.** FastAPI already emits OpenAPI from `Plan`; run `openapi-typescript` in CI so `Plan` and the route/method table are both generated. That kills all three cross-language findings at once — a wrong method or path becomes a type error at build time, not a 405 in production.
- **Fail the build on drift.** Commit the generated file and have CI regenerate and `git diff --exit-code`. A backend tier added without regenerating becomes a red build.
- **Pick one name for the concept.** `team` vs `workspace` is what made this invisible to search; crimes suggests `organization`, but any single name works. If the boundary name genuinely must differ, document the mapping in both files.
- **Make the Python side stop failing soft.** Type `change_team_plan(plan: Plan)` instead of `plan: str` so an unknown tier is a 422, and drop the `seats_for` default of `1` — a plan not in `SEATS_INCLUDED` should raise, not quietly grant one seat.

`crimes scan` can't tell you which side is *right* — it only proves the two closed sets disagree and that the disagreement is unguarded by tests. Confirming that `scale` is the intended new tier and `enterprise` is the stale one is a product call.
